resources.string: Scadangers is a local-first security companion. There is no account, backend, advertising or telemetry. Your device information stays on this device.

Without special access you can view basic device information, browse every screen and manage access. On Android 11 and later, installed-app visibility is limited by Android. Open Apps to review the visible installed-app inventory and local metadata findings.
All optional access can wait. Open a feature and choose Review access to see why it needs a permission before any Android prompt appears.

Optional access includes notifications, Bluetooth discovery, Wi-Fi scans, nearby Wi-Fi connections, local network discovery and VPN authorization. Skip any or all of these. You can review them later in each feature or in Settings. Denying access never blocks unrelated screens.

Granting access does not enable background monitoring. Installed-app scans start in Apps. No radio, network or background monitoring is implemented. Future monitoring will require separate, explicit consent.

App information supports local installed-app review. No runtime permission or Settings grant is available for package visibility. Android 11 and later filter which packages are visible; Scadangers queries launchable and automatically visible apps without broad package access. Other profiles are not scanned.

Open This device → Details for a limited, local security posture assessment. Public Android indicators and selected offline bulletins require no runtime permission or Google service. They do not establish overall device safety or provide privileged information.

Notification access would let a future alert feature notify you. Android 13 and later ask for runtime consent; older versions use app notification settings. Permission does not start monitoring. No alerts are generated in this version.

Bluetooth access would let future foreground discovery find nearby BLE devices. Android 12 and later request Nearby devices access. Older versions need location access and location services. Bluetooth scan results will not be used to infer location; some beacons may be filtered. This version does not scan. The Bluetooth radio must be enabled for future discovery.

Wi-Fi scan results can reveal location. Future foreground scans need location permission: approximate on Android 7–9, precise on Android 10 and later. Android 12 and later request approximate and precise together; approximate alone is insufficient. Location services must be on from Android 9. Nearby Wi-Fi permission does not replace location for scan results or starting scans. This version does not scan.

Selected nearby Wi-Fi connection APIs need Nearby devices consent on Android 13 and later and location access on older releases. This separate access does not authorize Wi-Fi scan results. No connections or discovery start in this version.

Broad local network access would allow future discovery of devices on your network. Android 17 requires local network runtime consent. Earlier releases have no separate runtime prompt for this access. Access is optional and does not begin discovery. This version sends no discovery traffic.

VPN authorization would allow future VPN-based traffic monitoring. Android allows one active VPN per profile: authorizing this app or enabling VPN-based monitoring may replace or disconnect your currently active Android VPN. Android shows a separate connection consent screen. This version only checks or requests authorization; it never establishes a VPN or monitors traffic.
Previously available access was revoked or disabled
Android needs your permission. You can decline and keep using other features.
Android may no longer show a permission prompt. Review access in app Settings if you want to enable it. You can also leave it off.
The required radio hardware is unavailable. Other app features remain usable.
Notifications are disabled in Android Settings. This check covers app-level access; individual notification channels may have their own settings when an alert feature is added.
Location services are off. You can choose to enable them in system Settings; this app will not change them automatically.
A separate Android VPN consent action is required. You may cancel it.
Your device or profile policy restricts VPN configuration. Contact your administrator if you need access.
This build is missing a required platform permission. Access is unavailable.
This Android version is outside the supported API range.
Access alone does not mean protection is active. Access requests start no scan, VPN service or background monitoring. Start installed-app scans in Apps.
Your access history or onboarding choices could not be saved or read. Access is unverified. Retry or continue using other screens.
Android access checks could not be completed. Access is unverified. Retry in Settings; other screens remain available.
Android could not open this permission or Settings screen. Access has not been enabled. You can review this app in system Settings.
